slides.say: A, B, C and D represent different digits, and each of them is a prime number. Given: A B plus B C is equal to C D. C is equal to what?

Prime digits only. [short pause] We'll solve it by plugging in the choices, organized trial and error. First, vertically, and an inventory. The prime digits are two, three, five and seven. Four letters, four different primes, so every one of them is used.
C is two or three? In the tens, A plus B, maybe with a carry, has to give C. But two different primes add up to at least two plus three, five. So choice numbers two and three are out.

C is seven? Then the ones are B plus seven. B two gives nine, and B three gives ten, and nine and zero aren't prime. B five gives twelve, so D is two and one carries. Then the tens, A plus five plus one is seven, so A is one. Not a prime. Out.
C is five. The tens, A plus B is five, so they're two and three. The ones, B plus five is D. B two gives seven, the prime that's left. So A is three, B is two, and D is seven.
Thirty-two plus twenty-five is fifty-seven. It works. Choice number four is our answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
